title: Adobe MAX 2026: Adobe Brings AI Agents To Photoshop, Premiere And Illustrator, Here's What They Can Do

detailed: The US-based software giant Adobe has announced new AI features across its Creative Cloud apps at Adobe MAX 2026.
The company is bringing its 'Creative Agent' to popular apps such as Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator, InDesign and After Effects.
The Adobe Creative Agent will power AI Assistants across these applications.
This will allow users to connect their preferred third-party AI agents with Adobe's creative tools.
sentences: The US-based software giant Adobe has announced new AI features across its Creative Cloud apps at Adobe MAX 2026.
The company is bringing its 'Creative Agent' to popular apps such as Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator, InDesign and After Effects.
With these new features, users can ask AI to handle multiple editing tasks through simple instructions instead of making every change manually.
The Adobe Creative Agent will power AI Assistants across these applications.
Users will be able to ask the agent to complete complex tasks through natural language prompts.
The idea is to make editing easier while allowing creators to remain in control of the final output.
The AI assistants are designed to understand what users want and help them carry out multiple steps within their creative projects.
In Premiere, the AI assistant will be able to apply effects across every clip in a sequence.
It can also track masked subjects throughout a video and adjust colour and exposure across an entire sequence.
This will help video editors save time on tasks that would otherwise require them to make changes to individual clips.
The software giant is also previewing local MCP integrations for Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and After Effects.
This will allow users to connect their preferred third-party AI agents with Adobe's creative tools.
These agents will be able to make changes directly to native project files stored on the user's computer.
Importantly, layers, vectors, bins and sequences will remain editable even after an AI agent makes changes.
This means creators can continue working on individual elements manually instead of relying completely on AI-generated output.
It also allows them to make further adjustments using the tools and features they are already familiar with.
The company says these updates are designed to help professional creators save time on repetitive tasks and focus more on their creative work.
Adobe is also looking to make its applications work with different AI assistants, giving users more flexibility in choosing the tools they want to use.
The AI Assistants are currently in beta across supported Creative Cloud applications, while the local MCP integrations are being previewed by Adobe.
